concepts.def: A tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Types of nuclear radiation with different penetration and ionising power.
Time for half the undecayed nuclei to decay.
Splitting a large nucleus, releasing energy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles & Radiation — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Particles & Radiation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Particles & Radiation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The quark composition of a neutron is:
options: uss
udd
uud
uuu

mcqs.q: Which of these is a lepton?
options: The proton
The neutron
The pion
The electron

mcqs.q: When a particle meets its antiparticle, they:
options: Annihilate, producing photons.
Form a stable atom.
Pass through each other unchanged.
Combine into a heavier quark.

mcqs.q: In the photoelectric effect, no electrons are emitted below the threshold frequency because:
options: Electrons are repelled by low-frequency light.
The metal melts first.
Each photon carries too little energy to overcome the work function.
The light is not bright enough.

mcqs.q: Is the proton a fundamental particle?
options: No — it is a baryon made of two up quarks and one down quark.
It was stored inside the nucleus all along.
No — protons are made of three electrons.
Yes — protons cannot be divided any further.

mcqs.q: In beta-minus decay, where does the emitted electron come from?
options: It was stored inside the nucleus all along.
No — protons are made of three electrons.
It is an orbital electron ejected from its shell.
It is created when a neutron changes into a proton, together with an antineutrino.

mcqs.q: Does brighter (more intense) light give each photoelectron more kinetic energy?
options: It was stored inside the nucleus all along.
Yes — brighter light means more energetic electrons.
Yes — bright light heats the electrons until they boil off.
No — intensity increases the number emitted; only a higher frequency raises the maximum kinetic energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photoelectric effect”?
options: Light above a threshold frequency releases electrons from a metal surface — key evidence for the photon model.
A quantum of electromagnetic radiation carrying energy E = hf.
A fundamental particle not made of quarks, such as the electron and the neutrino.
Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photon”?
options: Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.
A quantum of electromagnetic radiation carrying energy E = hf.
Light above a threshold frequency releases electrons from a metal surface — key evidence for the photon model.
A particle made of quarks that feels the strong interaction; baryons contain three quarks, mesons a quark-antiquark pair.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Lepton”?
options: A fundamental particle; up and down quarks combine to form protons (uud) and neutrons (udd).
Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.
A particle made of quarks that feels the strong interaction; baryons contain three quarks, mesons a quark-antiquark pair.
A fundamental particle not made of quarks, such as the electron and the neutrino.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quark”?
options: Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.
A quantum of electromagnetic radiation carrying energy E = hf.
A fundamental particle; up and down quarks combine to form protons (uud) and neutrons (udd).
A fundamental particle not made of quarks, such as the electron and the neutrino.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Antiparticle”?
options: A quantum of electromagnetic radiation carrying energy E = hf.
Light above a threshold frequency releases electrons from a metal surface — key evidence for the photon model.
A fundamental particle; up and down quarks combine to form protons (uud) and neutrons (udd).
Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hadron”?
options: A particle made of quarks that feels the strong interaction; baryons contain three quarks, mesons a quark-antiquark pair.
Has the same mass as its particle but opposite charge; a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate into photons.
Light above a threshold frequency releases electrons from a metal surface — key evidence for the photon model.
A fundamental particle not made of quarks, such as the electron and the neutrino.

mcqs.q: A photon has frequency 5×10¹⁴ Hz and h ≈ 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J s. What is its energy, in units of 10⁻¹⁹ J?

free_texts.q: Type the key term for a particle made of quarks that feels the strong interaction.
free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.

sequence.def: Rest energy 0.511 MeV — lightest charged lepton
Rest energy 105.7 MeV; a heavier lepton
Rest energy 493.7 MeV; a strange meson
Rest energy 939.6 MeV; just heavier than the proton
